title: D-amino acid aminotransferase1 regulates grain chalkiness in rice by modulating endoplasmic reticulum stress response

venue.name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

abstract: D-amino acids are key components of the bacterial cell wall and play important roles in neural communication and inflammatory responses in animals. However, knowledge about D-amino acid metabolism and physiological functions in plants is limited. Here, we isolated and characterized a rice D-amino acid aminotransferase1, OsDAAT1, which maternally regulates rice grain chalkiness through map-based cloning and a subsequent complementation test. We found that OsDAAT1 is highly expressed in the vascular tissue of rice nodes and is capable of interconverting different D-amino acids in vitro. Mutation of OsDAAT1 results in elevated D-alanine levels in stems, nodes, and developing grains. The disruption of D-amino acid metabolism subsequently leads to significantly altered peptide/protein isomerization, including some key enzymes involved in starch and protein biosynthesis. These changes trigger severe endoplasmic reticulum stress and ultimately leads to chalky grains. Furthermore, we identified OsDAAT1Hap1as a low-chalkiness haplotype, and historical frequency analysis suggests that OsDAAT1 may have undergone selection during rice domestication. Overall, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized role in D-amino acid metabolism in plants and facilitate the practical use of OsDAAT1 in grain appearance quality improvement in rice.

narrative_llm:
Short impact summary

This PNAS article identifies OsDAAT1 as a maternally acting regulator of rice grain chalkiness, linking D-amino acid metabolism to endoplasmic reticulum stress response in plants. The work has already seen one documented scholarly reuse and one citation in the literature, suggesting early but focused uptake in rice genetics and grain-quality research.

Full narrative

The study advances a new mechanistic connection between amino-acid metabolism and grain quality in rice. By map-based cloning and complementation, the authors characterize OsDAAT1 and show that it influences chalkiness through modulation of endoplasmic reticulum stress response. That framing matters because grain chalkiness is a key quality trait in rice, and the paper offers a specific gene-level explanation that can inform downstream breeding and functional studies.

The article’s early influence is concentrated but discernible. OpenAlex records one citation so far, from a 2026 article in Euphytica on rice grain chalkiness that builds on bulked segregant analysis and KASP marker work. The citing record comes from China and sits squarely in crop genetics and rice improvement, which suggests the paper is already being used as part of an active research conversation around chalkiness mechanisms and candidate-gene discovery.

Beyond citation, the reuse record shows one documented downstream mention in Europe PMC, indicating that the article has entered the biomedical literature infrastructure even as broader community attention remains sparse. There are no recorded online mentions in the available event-data sources, so the visible footprint is still mainly scholarly rather than public-facing.

The article is well supported by a substantial China-based funding portfolio, including national and provincial programs tied to agricultural research and seed industry revitalization. Combined with its publication in a high-profile venue and hybrid open-access availability, the record suggests a work positioned for applied significance in rice biology, with impact likely to grow as more studies test OsDAAT1 and related stress-response pathways in grain-quality improvement.
